(p-255) Surah al-Nasr

It is Madani, by the consensus of scholars.

In Muslim's collection, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, it is related that it was the last surah to be revealed in its entirety.

(p-256) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When the help of Allah comes and victory﴾ means: His aid against the enemies. And "the victory" is the conquest of Makkah. Al-Hasan said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makkah, the Arabs said: 'Now that Muhammad has prevailed over the people of the Sacred Precinct, and Allah has protected them from the companions of the Elephant, you have no power to resist him.' So they entered the religion of Allah in multitudes." Abu 'Ubayda said: "Afwaj" means groups, in separate bands.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise﴾ — concerning this there are two opinions.

One of them: it means the prayer (al-salah). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

(p-257) The second: it means the well-known tasbih (glorification). This was said by a group of the exegetes. The exegetes said: His own death was announced to him by the revelation of this surah, and he was informed that his term had drawn near, so he was commanded to glorify and seek forgiveness, so that his life would be concluded with an increase in righteous deeds. Ibn 'Abbas said: "﴿When the help of Allah comes and victory﴾: a summons from Allah, and a farewell from the world." Qatadah said: "He lived two years after the revelation of this surah."
